title: QUIC double-free during concurrent connection resets in a multithreaded static OpenSSL build
body: I am using OpenSSL 3.5.2 on Linux x86_64 with GCC 13. During intensive testing with multiple concurrent QUIC connections, AddressSanitizer sporadically reports a double-free when one connection is reset by its peer. One thread frees the memory through OpenSSL error handling and another later frees the same address. The test rapidly creates and tears down connections: the server accepts about 4–5 KB from the data connection and closes it while a separate signaling connection handles control messages.

symptoms_visible: During intensive concurrent QUIC connection resets, AddressSanitizer sporadically reports an attempted double-free.
The first report shows one connection thread freeing the allocation through ERR_clear_error and the signaling connection thread later freeing the same address through ERR_pop_to_mark.
N0.label: N0 concurrent QUIC double-free reported

symptoms_visible: With OpenSSL 3.6 alpha1, AddressSanitizer still reports a double-free between the signaling and data-connection threads.
N1.label: N1 newer branch also reproduces

symptoms_visible: The double-free occurs while two separate QUIC connections, each with its own socket and default stream, are active.
N2.label: N2 connection and thread architecture clarified

symptoms_visible: After changing every SSL connection so creation, I/O, shutdown, and destruction all happen in its dedicated main QUIC thread, AddressSanitizer still reports the double-free.
N3_x.label: N3_x same-thread lifecycle aftermath

symptoms_visible: The isolated implementation still produces AddressSanitizer double-free reports on 3.6.0-beta1.
The added port-thread checks do not print their abort messages before AddressSanitizer reports the failure.
My standalone reproducer fails consistently on my Linux systems, while it does not fail on my colleague's Mac.
N4.label: N4 isolation and port hypotheses tested

symptoms_visible: The reproducer crashes when linked with the OpenSSL libraries produced by the exact failing static configuration, but runs normally with the dynamically linked build.
In the failing build, my logging repeatedly prints CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local(none) with the same key.
After rebuilding without insisting on the static-only setup, I no longer see the problem.
N5.label: N5 non-threaded backend exposed

symptoms_visible: With an OpenSSL build that uses the threaded implementation, the concurrent QUIC stress test runs without the AddressSanitizer double-free or cross-connection error behavior.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with thread-enabled build

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this with the current 3.6 prerelease branch and paste the raw AddressSanitizer result?
Please rerun the stress test against 3.6 alpha1 and tell me exactly what ASAN reports.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it with 3.6 alpha1. ASAN again says 'attempting double-free'; cas_qm_signalin frees it through ERR_pop_to_mark, while the report says the same allocation was previously freed by cas_qs_0_0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I ran the same stress test for an extended period on 3.6 alpha1 and saw neither a crash nor any connection receiving another connection's errors.
The same double-free occurs on 3.6 alpha1, but the thread numbers and allocation address differ.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's system: participant1 requested a 3.6 alpha1 run; the reporter returned raw ASAN stacks showing the failure remained.

question_patterns: Are signaling and data separate QUIC connections or streams on one connection, and how many sockets are polled?
Please describe whether the threads share a connection and how many file descriptors are passed to select.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: They are two separate RFC 9000 QUIC connections, not streams on one connection. I monitor two QUIC sockets with select().

counterfactual_candidates.answer: They are two streams on one QUIC connection, and both worker threads call OpenSSL on that same SSL object.
They remain separate QUIC connections, but I poll the two sockets with poll() instead of select().

question_patterns: How many streams does each of those connections use?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Each separate QUIC connection uses only its one default stream.

question_patterns: Do the connection threads share any SSL, BIO, SSL_CTX, or QUIC connection object?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The connection threads do not share QUIC connection objects. Each has its own SSL connection and BIO resources, and the socket watcher only uses select and queues signals; it does not call OpenSSL.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c9, reporter's architecture: participant2 distinguished separate connections from streams and elicited the socket/object layout. The reporter additionally disclosed that creation, use, and destruction could initially occur in different threads.

solution.intent: Restructure the application so each SSL object is created, used, shut down, and freed by one dedicated thread.
solution.concrete_example: Move SSL_new, SSL_connect, every SSL_read_ex or SSL_write_ex call, SSL_shutdown, and SSL_free into the connection's cas_qm thread; let the watcher thread only poll the socket and exchange queue signals.

edges.comment: Issue c7-c12 and c18-c20, reporter's system: participant2 proposed same-thread creation/use/destruction as a workaround. The reporter implemented that persistent architecture change, but detailed ASAN reports still showed the double-free.

question_patterns: Can you rerun the fully isolated implementation on the 3.6 beta branch and provide the complete ASAN stacks?
Please test a current prerelease build with debug symbols and paste both the current and previous free stacks.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On 3.6.0-beta1 I still got 'AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free'. One run frees through raise_error in quic_tls.c in cas_qm_signalin, and the earlier free is reported in another connection thread during certificate decoding.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The fully isolated implementation runs cleanly on 3.6 beta1, and ASAN reports no memory errors.

question_patterns: Can you run the proposed instrumentation patch and report whether one of its explicit abort checks fires before ASAN?
Please test the diagnostic patch and paste the first failure it prints.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I applied the diagnostic patch to both reported runs. None of the patch's explicit abort checks fired; AddressSanitizer still aborted on the double-free.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The diagnostic patch immediately prints that a thread is accessing a port created by another thread and aborts there.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a standalone client and server that maintainers can run?
Please share a minimal reproducer with exact startup instructions.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made a standalone reproducer with a Go QUIC service and C OpenSSL client: https://github.com/reporter/reproducer/tree/main/openSSL. On my Linux environment it reproduces every time.

edges.comment: Issue c18-c24 and c27-c42, reporter's isolated implementation: the reporter supplied fuller beta ASAN traces, ran participant3's port instrumentation without its checks firing, and later published the standalone reproducer. The reporter also volunteered the Linux-versus-Mac observation.

question_patterns: Can you provide the complete configdata.pm --dump output for the OpenSSL build used by the reproducer?
Please share the exact OpenSSL configuration used for the failing executable.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I uploaded the complete output as OpenSSLConfigData.txt and used that same configuration for the failing reproducer builds.

question_patterns: Can you compare the reproducer using the exact failing library configuration with a normally linked build and report the raw behavior of each?
Please check the executable's linked libraries and rerun the same client with both build layouts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the exact configuration that produces the static OpenSSL libraries, the client reproduces the memory errors. With the dynamically linked shared-library build, the same client runs without the error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The double-free occurs identically with both static and dynamically linked OpenSSL builds.
The static run fails after a different number of connection cycles, while the dynamic run still completes normally.

edges.comment: Issue c27-c32 and c43-c50, reporter and maintainer reproductions folded into one simulated user side: the reporter supplied the requested configuration, while participant3 established that the exact static configuration reproduces and the shared-library build does not. The reporter then independently logged CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local resolving to threads_none and reported that a non-static-only rebuild removed the problem.

solution.intent: Reconfigure and rebuild OpenSSL with threading enabled so the multithreaded application uses the platform thread-local implementation rather than threads_none, then rerun the concurrent QUIC stress test. Do not treat static linkage or no-shared alone as the root cause.
solution.concrete_example: Inspect the generated configuration to find what selected crypto/threads_none.c, remove the option or build-script behavior that disabled threads, and rebuild OpenSSL. A static no-shared build is acceptable if it retains pthread support; verify that the rebuilt library no longer dispatches CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local to the none implementation, then rerun the reset stress test under ASAN.
solution.inference_hint: The decisive inference is not that static OpenSSL libraries are inherently unsafe. The failing build resolves CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local to crypto/threads_none.c while the application concurrently uses OpenSSL from many threads. That removes the per-thread isolation expected by ERR_STATE and explains the apparent cross-thread error-state sharing. The maintainers explicitly note that no-shared alone should not disable threads, so the build configuration or script selecting threads_none must be corrected.

edges.comment: Issue c48-c52, final accepted diagnostic chain: participant3 reproduced only with the exact static configuration, the reporter observed threads_none in that build and reported no further issue after rebuilding differently, and maintainers clarified that static/no-shared itself should not disable threading. The scored fix is restoring thread support, not merely switching linkage format.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final root cause as an OpenSSL build selecting the non-threaded threads_none implementation while the application uses OpenSSL concurrently, defeating the expected per-thread error-state isolation.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the exact-build comparison and the reporter's CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local(none) logging, not inferred solely from QUIC reset symptoms or the original ASAN stack.
Must recommend rebuilding OpenSSL with platform thread support and must not claim that static linkage or Configure no-shared inherently disables threading.
Must not present same-thread SSL creation, use, and destruction as the fix; the reporter implemented that architecture and the double-free persisted.
Must not retain the shared QUIC_PORT or stream-conclude race hypotheses as the root cause; the diagnostic port checks did not fire and the proposed ordering patch had no impact.
Must ask the reporter to verify the rebuilt thread-enabled library with the concurrent reset stress test under AddressSanitizer before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical C developer building a multithreaded video application; comfortable with OpenSSL QUIC APIs, custom build scripts, sanitizers, source instrumentation, cross-compilation, and producing standalone reproducers, but initially uncertain about OpenSSL's build-time threading backend.
persona_hint.communication_style: Very detailed, persistent, and cooperative; provides long code and stack dumps, develops hypotheses openly, corrects translation misunderstandings, and responds appreciatively when maintainers reproduce the issue.
